chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Ahmad ibn al-Jahm al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Yazid, from some of his companions, who said:

I was behind Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) on al-Safa or on al-Marwah, and he did not add more than two words: 'O God, I ask You for good opinion of You in every state, and sincerity of intention in reliance upon You.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the hills in Mecca
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwah, the second hill in Mecca
key_terms.حُسْنَ الظَّنِّ: Good opinion or expectation of God

ai.seo_question: What was the short supplication recited by Imam Musa al-Kazim during Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the spiritual etiquette of the Imams during the pilgrimage rites of Sa'i, specifically noting Imam Musa al-Kazim’s (AS) practice near Safa or Marwah. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *Husn al-Zann* (optimistic trust in God) and *Sidq al-Niyyah* (sincerity of intention) as foundational pillars for accepting worship and divine proximity.
